title: Model brief can call a failed screen clean: SCREENS and GAPS sections are never checked
scenario: Report where sanctions-lists failed (2 of 2 lookups errored, screen status 'failed'). The model writes '• Sanctions and watchlists: no match in Sanctions lists' and '• Every screen answered in full.' Both lines are kept (mode 'ai'). Its bottom line leaves out the silent screen and passes. GAPS also keeps an uncited '• She was investigated by the FCA for insider trading in 2017.'
fix: Do not take PUBLIC-RECORD SCREENS from the model: always use screenLines(report). In BOTTOM LINE, always add the assembled silent-screens sentence when silentScreens() is not empty. In GAPS, drop an uncited line unless it matches NO_CLAIM or a coverage label.
verifyNote: Reproduced. With the sanctions screen 'failed', the model's '• Sanctions and watchlists: no match in Sanctions lists' and '• Every screen answered in full.' are kept, because SCREENS and GAPS are outside FACT_SECTIONS. The uncited FCA claim in GAPS is kept too. The bottom line loses the silent-screens sentence, and nothing puts it back.
betterFix: Always set PUBLIC-RECORD SCREENS to screenLines(report), ignoring the model. Append the assembled silent-screens sentence to BOTTOM LINE whenever silentScreens() is not empty and the kept text does not name each label. In GAPS, keep an uncited line only if it matches an anchored NO_CLAIM or names a coverage or screen label.

title: Name-only or invented red flags pass by adding one tied citation; the overlap test needs one 5-letter stem
scenario: Reproduced, all kept in mode 'ai': (a) RED FLAGS '• Arrested for burglary in Leeds in 2018 [Source 3 (possible)] [Source 2 (tied bio)]'. ns.some(tied) passes, and sharesWords matches against the namesake record itself. (b) '• Sued by Acme Bank for embezzlement in 2018 [Source 2]' passes because the bio mentions 'Acme'. (c) BOTTOM LINE 'She was convicted of embezzlement at Acme Bank in 2015 [Source 2]' gets no content check at all.
fix: In RED FLAGS, compute sharesWords only over tied, non-ownStatement cited records, and drop the possible citations from the line. Require at least two distinctive stems, including one event word (charged, sued, convicted, fined and similar) present in the record. Run the same check on BOTTOM LINE sentences that carry event words.
verifyNote: Reproduced in mode 'ai'. With a name-only record (n4) in sections, '• Arrested for burglary in Leeds [Source 4] [Source 2]' is kept: tied() passes on the bio, and sharesWords matches the namesake's own words. 'Sued by Acme Bank…[Source 2]' is kept on 'acme'. A bottom-line 'convicted of embezzlement…[Source 2]' gets no content check.
betterFix: In RED FLAGS and in bottom-line sentences that hold event words, strip the possible and assumedTie citations first, then run sharesWords only over the remaining tied records that are not ownStatement. Require that a record also holds an event stem (charg/sued/convi/fined/arres/indic/settl…) and one other distinctive stem. If that fails, drop the unit.

title: Uncited accusations pass the fact-section check through the NO_CLAIM and LABEL escapes
scenario: In RED FLAGS, '• Convicted of embezzlement in 2015; no records of an appeal were found.' is kept with no citation, because NO_CLAIM matches 'no records' anywhere in the line. In BOTTOM LINE, 'Convicted of wire fraud in Ohio in 2016:' is kept because it fits LABEL (short text ending in a colon).
fix: Anchor NO_CLAIM to the whole line (e.g. ^[•\s]*(?:None found|No ... found)\b[^;]*$) and reject a line holding an event word. Allow LABEL only outside BOTTOM LINE, and only for the known labels ('About the company:', 'To confirm with the person:', 'Only if this is the right person').
verifyNote: Reproduced. '• Convicted of embezzlement in 2015; no records of an appeal were found.' is kept uncited in RED FLAGS, because NO_CLAIM is unanchored. The LABEL escape needs a bottom-line sentence that ends in a colon. That is narrower than claimed, but the regex allows it.
betterFix: Make NO_CLAIM match the whole unit (anchored, and no event stem anywhere in it). Allow LABEL only outside BOTTOM LINE, and only for the known labels ('About the company', 'To confirm with the person', 'Only if this is the right person').

title: Matters that hold only if this is the right person are silently dropped from the AI brief
scenario: No company typed; ifRightPerson holds 'Jane Roe of Zeta sued for fraud by investors' (assumedTie). The model follows the prompt and writes it under RED FLAGS after 'Only if this is the right person:', plus one bottom-line sentence. keepUnit drops both, because tied() excludes assumedTie. The AI brief is accepted with RED FLAGS reading 'None found… Only if this is the right person:' and nothing under it.
fix: In RED FLAGS, accept assumedTie citations for lines that follow an 'Only if this is the right person' label, and say so in the prompt. Or, when report.ifRightPerson is not empty, always add the assembled ifRightPerson block and its bottom-line sentence to the AI brief.
verifyNote: Reproduced. The model writes the assumedTie matter under 'Only if this is the right person:' as the prompt asks, and keepUnit drops it because tied() excludes assumedTie. The AI brief is accepted with a dangling label and nothing under it. The assembled ifRightPerson block is never put back.
betterFix: After the checks, replace the model's 'Only if this is the right person' block with the assembled one whenever report.ifRightPerson is not empty. Keep the assembled bottom-line sentence that counts these matters. Do not loosen tied() for other lines.

title: Fraud amounts, valuations and stock values shown as 'latest funding'; an SEC charge release shown as a filing that 'confirms' a funding round
scenario: Rebuilt Trevor Milton r9: BOTTOM LINE says 'the latest funding on record is $600M (2023-12-18) [72]', where 72 is NY Post '…four years in prison for $600M fraud'. WHAT CHECKS OUT says 'An SEC filing confirms Nikola's funding round: $1 billion' citing SEC press release 'SEC Charges Founder of Nikola Corp. With Fraud'. Jack Zhang's brief gives '$15.9 billion' as the latest round. Root cause: round-less amounts from companyFacts.js.
fix: In the brief, state a funding entry as a round only when it has a round label or comes from a Form D (data.form==='D'). In whatChecksOut, require the cited record to be an offering filing whose quote contains the amount. officialKind should call SEC press releases 'an SEC press release'. Also fix the amount extraction in companyFacts.js.
verifyNote: Rebuilt from r9 with the current buildCompanyFacts. Nikola's funding shows $600M from 'gets four years in prison for $600M fraud' (RAISE matches 'gets'), $3.1B from a stock-forfeit headline and $1 billion from an SEC charge release plus Milton's new AI-plane raise. WHAT CHECKS OUT says 'An SEC filing confirms Nikola's funding round: $1 billion'. Zhang's round shows $15.9B.
betterFix: In companyFacts, drop round-less amounts unless the sentence holds a funding noun (funding, round, financing, investment) and no crime, fine or settlement word, and drop 'gets'/'got' from RAISE. In whatChecksOut, confirm funding only from a Form D whose quote holds the amount. In officialKind, call an SEC press release 'an SEC press release'.

title: COMPANY section prints page navigation text and undated, conflicting valuation headlines
scenario: Jack Zhang r9 COMPANY bullet: '…amid $11 billion valuation Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer Help using this website - Accessibility statement Today's Paper…'. Eric Glyman r9 lists four valuations ($60B, $44B, $30B+, $32B) as raw headlines, two of them ending ' - CNBC.' / ' - saastr.com.'. They are undated and unordered, so the reader cannot tell which is current.
fix: Filter standing text that holds site-chrome phrases (skip to, accessibility statement, today's paper, cookie, sign in). Render standing as kind, value and the cited record's date, newest first, and strip a trailing ' - Publisher'. Fix clipAround in companyFacts.js too.
verifyNote: Rebuilt Zhang COMPANY: '…amid $11 billion valuation Skip to navigation Skip to content … Today's Paper…'. Glyman shows four valuation headlines, two ending ' - CNBC.' and ' - saastr.com.'. reportCompanyFacts drops the standing date, so the brief cannot order or date them.
betterFix: Keep kind, value and date in reportCompanyFacts. In companyFacts, cut sentences at site-chrome phrases and strip a trailing ' - Publisher'. In the brief, show one line per kind (the newest value with its date), the others as earlier figures.

title: COMPANY lists a domain that an earlier holder registered as the company's web domain
scenario: Trevor Milton r9: COMPANY shows '• Web domains: trevormilton.com [Source 171]'. Record 171 has data.earlierHolder true and the title 'first registered 2007-01-24, by an earlier holder (Nikola was founded in 2015)'. whatChecksOut excludes earlierHolder records, but the COMPANY line does not.
fix: In assembleSections' company list, keep a domain only when at least one cited record has no data.earlierHolder (use byN). Apply the same filter in companyFacts.js.
verifyNote: companyNames adds every non-possible domain-history record. earlierHolder is set only in buildReport's mapping, after the facts are built. So the rebuilt Milton COMPANY lists 'Web domains: trevormilton.com' (registered 2007; Nikola was founded in 2015), which is his personal domain, not the company's.
betterFix: In assembleSections, keep a domain only when one cited record (byN) is not earlierHolder. Better still, pass the founded year into companyNames and skip domains registered more than a year before it.

title: Bottom line names the most serious matter without its latest outcome (Milton's pardon is missing)
scenario: Trevor Milton r9: the bottom line reads 'the most serious: Trevor Milton Sentenced To Four Years In Prison… (2023-12-18)'. The 2025 presidential pardon (red flag 8, record 10) is never connected to it. Even when f.outcome exists (a dismissed suit, for example), line 1620 omits it, although the prompt asks for the latest outcome.
fix: Add '; latest outcome: …' from flags[0].outcome to the bottom-line sentence, as flagLine does. Upstream, attach pardon, acquittal and dismissal records as outcomes to the matter they resolve (report owner).
verifyNote: Line 1620 never reads flags[0].outcome, while flagLine does, so the bottom line states the most serious matter without its outcome even when a record gives one. The Milton pardon gap is mainly upstream: no outcome is attached to his flags.
betterFix: Reuse flagLine's outcome fragment in the bottom-line sentence. Separately, in report.js, attach pardon, acquittal, dismissal and vacated records as the outcome of the matter they resolve, by matterKey or docket.

title: Founder questions ask about third-party press rewrites, and ask for 'court documents' for press pieces
scenario: Questions produced: 'Ask what changed and why: cnbc.com page: bio rewritten between 2025-03 and 2026-01' (Milton), 'fortune.com page…' (Glyman) and 'clay.com…' (Zhang). Jack Zhang also gets 'Ask for… its final court or regulator documents: Career, as told on afr.com: …defies US attacks'. Milton's three redFlag questions all concern the same case, using up slots.
fix: Build change questions only from claimChanges with field in (title, role, dates, headline) or on the person's own pages. Use the court/regulator wording only for official-record or litigation/regulatory flags, and a 'what is your account of…' wording for press. Merge questions for the same matterKey.
verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Ask what changed and why: cnbc.com page: bio rewritten…' (Milton) and 'clay.com page' (Zhang). Zhang gets 'final court or regulator documents' for an afr.com career article. Milton's three redFlag questions cover one prosecution.
betterFix: Build change questions only from title, role or date changes, or from the person's own pages. Use the court-documents wording only for official litigation or regulatory flags, and ask for their account otherwise. Group redFlags by matterKey before taking three. Also fix upstream why 'Career, as told on…' records become red flags.

title: A confirmed criminal record vanishes from red flags when its headline does not name the person
scenario: Confirmed press record, high severity. Title: 'Fintech startup CEO pleads guilty to wire fraud'. Quote: 'Jane Roe, founder and CEO of Zetafold, pleaded guilty...'. Result: no red flag, no namesake entry, seriousRecords 0, so the summary reads '0 red flags'. Real r9 Zhang run: confirmed medium Forbes record #2 about the China data allegations is dropped the same way.
fix: Use aboutThem only to filter encyclopaedia or roundup pages (isWikiOther, data.wikiKind). Otherwise also accept a record whose quote names the person in full (subject.hasName) in the sentence that reports the serious event. Never drop a confirmed or likely serious record from every list: if it fails the test, keep it as a red flag marked 'mentioned in passing'.
evidence: zzReview test A: totals.redFlags 0, seriousRecords 0. r9/jack-zhang-airwallex rebuilt: record 2 is confirmed, medium, not flagged.
verifyNote: Reproduced. A confirmed high-severity press record, headline 'Fintech startup CEO pleads guilty...' with a quote naming Jane Roe, gives redFlags 0 and seriousRecords 0. aboutThem (line 822) tests only the title. Zhang r9 #2 (confirmed, medium) is also absent from every list.
betterFix: Have aboutThem reject only when no sentence of the quote names the person (subject.hasName) together with the event (eventOf on that sentence), or when isWikiOther is true. If a confirmed or likely serious record still fails, keep it as a red flag marked 'mentioned in passing' rather than dropping it from every list.

title: Acquittals, dismissals and pardons never attach to their matter, so the matter stays high with no outcome
scenario: DOJ 'Jane Roe indicted on wire fraud charges' (2021-02, high), then 'Jury acquits Jane Roe' (2022-06). finding.js grades exculpatory records low and sets data.outcome. The report only groups medium or high records, and only within 31 days and one event tag. Result: a high red flag with no outcome. Milton r9: the 'Trump pardons' record is its own red flag, and the sentencing flag has no pardon.
fix: After building matters, scan every tied record that has data.outcome, whatever its severity or date, and attach it to the matter it ends. Match on the same person, a shared docket or distinctive headline words, and a later date. Then lower the matter's severity for acquitted or dismissed (as finding.js does) and show the outcome.
evidence: zzReview test B: redFlags[0] has severity high and no outcome. Rebuilt r9 Milton: no red flag carries an outcome; #10 'Trump pardons...' is a separate high flag.
verifyNote: Reproduced. finding.js grades an acquittal 'low', so it never enters serious, and the indictment flag stays high with outcome null. In rebuilt Milton, the pardon is its own flag (#10, event tag 'pardon'), and sentencing flag #1 carries no outcome.
betterFix: After the matters are built, attach every tied record with data.outcome (any severity) that is dated later to a red flag of the same whoOf and a compatible event (charges, conviction or sentence), matched by docket or shared headline words. Pardon matters fold into the conviction or sentence matter. Lower the severity for acquitted or dismissed, as gradeByOutcome does.

title: Grouped page takes the severity of a name-only copy, so a benign confirmed page becomes a high red flag
scenario: Page reader (confirmed, info): 'Jane Roe is the founder and CEO of Zetafold'. Web-search snippet of the same URL (possible, high): 'John Doe was convicted of fraud'. groupPages keeps the confirmed lead and gives it the highest severity in the group. Result: red flag #1 'Zetafold team', high, quoting a benign bio line. Another person's matter is pinned on the founder.
fix: Take severity only from members tied at least as strongly as the lead (never from a 'possible' copy). When a tied member is more severe, make that member the lead, so the quote shown supports the flag.
evidence: zzReview test C: redFlags [{t:'Zetafold team', sev:'high'}], copiesMerged 1. Milton r9: #13 Wikipedia 'Career' was raised from info to high by a copy.
verifyNote: Reproduced. Line 569 takes the maximum severity across the group, including a 'possible' copy. The result is the 'Zetafold team' red flag, high, quoting a benign bio line.
betterFix: Compute severity only from members whose TIE_ORDER is at least the lead's. If a tied member is more severe, it becomes the lead so the quote shown supports the flag. A severe 'possible' copy stays listed in alsoIn and never raises the group.

title: One matter splits into many red flags (Milton: 35 red flags) when reports are undated, dated to the year only, or worded differently
scenario: Rebuilt r9 Trevor Milton report: totals.redFlags is 35. Separate flags for the sentencing (#1, plus undated Reddit #54 and #55), the conviction (#32 dated 2022-10-19; #40 'Guilty of Defrauding Investors' 2022-10-14; Wikidata #3 and #4 dated '2022'), and the charges (#6; Reddit #56). The cause: undated records become 'single|id', year-only dates key as '2022', and 'Guilty of' matches no event.
fix: Add a second pass that merges a tied serious record into an existing tied matter with the same event tag when they share at least one distinctive headline word. Treat an undated or year-only record as compatible with any window in its year. Add a bare '\bguilty\b' to the conviction pattern. Add a test asserting Milton has fewer than 12 red flags.
evidence: Rebuilt r9/trevor-milton-nikola.json with the current buildReport: 35 red flags; per-flag titles and dates were printed and inspected.
verifyNote: Reproduced. Rebuilt r9 Milton gives 35 red flags. The conviction is split across #3, #4 (year-only), #32, #40 ('Guilty of' matches no event), #30 and #14; the sentencing across #1, #54 and #55 (undated); the charges across #6 and #56.
betterFix: Add 'guilty' to the conviction tag. In dateWindows and matterKey, let undated or year-only tied records of a RARE_EVENT for the same whoOf join that event's single window, or the window in their year when there is one. Merge only on rare events, not on lawsuits. Add a regression test that caps Milton's flags.

title: A product launch year becomes the founding year, and the company's own domain is relabelled 'by an earlier holder'
scenario: No founding fact in companyFacts. A confirmed record says 'Zetafold launched its bill pay product in 2022'. A domain-history record shows zetafold.com registered 2019-03-02. Result: the domain record is retitled 'first registered 2019-03-02, by an earlier holder (Zetafold was founded in 2022)' and taken off the timeline. That is a false statement about the company, and the brief will not let 'what checks out' rest on it.
fix: Drop 'launched' and 'started' from the regex, or require the company itself as their object ('Zetafold was launched in', 'started Zetafold in'), never 'Zetafold launched <something>'. Require two agreeing records before marking a domain as an earlier holder's.
evidence: zzReview test H printed 'zetafold.com: first registered 2019-03-02, by an earlier holder (Zetafold was founded in 2022)'.
verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Zetafold launched its bill pay product in 2022' sets foundedYear to 2022, and the zetafold.com 2019 record is retitled 'by an earlier holder' and taken off the timeline.
betterFix: In the first regex, allow only '<Co> was (founded|started|launched|incorporated|established)' or '<Co>, founded in'. Never allow '<Co> launched <object>'. Require two agreeing records, or a profile or companyFacts year, before marking a domain as an earlier holder's.

title: A real title change on the person's own LinkedIn is dropped when the profile address has the usual numeric suffix
scenario: Archived change record (likely), field 'headline', page linkedin.com/in/jane-roe-4b2a17, before 'CTO at Paribus', after 'CEO at Zetafold'. ownPage needs a path segment exactly equal to a slug candidate ('jane-roe'), and a headline never contains the full name. Result: claimChanges is empty.
fix: In ownPage, also accept a segment that starts with a slug candidate followed by '-' and an alphanumeric suffix (or digits) on profile hosts such as linkedin.com/in. Alternatively, accept CLAIM_FIELDS changes on a record already graded confirmed or likely when the page is a profile page.
verifyNote: Reproduced. A likely headline change on linkedin.com/in/jane-roe-4b2a17 gives claimChanges 0: ownPage needs an exact slug match, and a headline does not name the person.
betterFix: In ownPage, also accept a segment matching ^<slug>(-[a-z0-9]{2,12})?$ when it sits under linkedin.com/in or another profile path. A CLAIM_FIELDS change on a record already graded confirmed or likely can count as own.

title: Real company news leaves the numbered report as 'word only' for an ordinary-word company
scenario: Company 'Ramp', records graded 'company' by news search. These are moved out of the report into wordOnly: "Ramp's new AI agents take on expense fraud", 'Stripe and Ramp partner on bill pay', 'Inside Ramp: the spend management upstart'. 'Ramp raises...' and 'Ramp acquires...' are kept. This thins the company picture the owner complained about.
fix: In ordinaryWordOnly, demote to possible and keep the record numbered, rather than removing it as word-only, when the text has business context (a possessive followed by a product word, 'X and Ramp partner', a fintech or startup noun nearby). Move only records with an explicit non-company use (a boat ramp, 'ramp up') to wordOnly. Or widen names.js companyMention for possessives and 'and <Company>' partnerships.
evidence: zzReview test J: wordOnly listed those three headlines next to 'Boat ramp closed' and 'Ramp up production'.
verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Ramp's new AI agents...', 'Stripe and Ramp partner...' and 'Inside Ramp: the spend management upstart' go to wordOnly next to 'Boat ramp closed'. They are still listed with a reason, so nothing is silent, but the company picture thins.
betterFix: Widen names.js companyMention, shared with the identity matcher so the two still agree, to cover a possessive followed by a noun, '<Org> and <Co> partner', and 'Inside <Co>:'. Do not special-case report.js.

title: A judge 'sanctioning' a party outranks a criminal conviction in red-flag order
scenario: Two tied records: 'Jane Roe convicted of securities fraud' (high, 2022) and 'Judge sanctions Jane Roe over discovery abuse in Zetafold contract suit' (medium, 2020). The headline word 'sanctions' gives weight 6, above conviction's 5, so the discovery sanction is listed first. Any tied report in `more` that mentions 'sanctions' (Russia sanctions, for example) lifts its matter the same way.
fix: Give weight 6 only from the source or category (LIST_SOURCES, category 'sanctions', a debarment source). In headlines, count only list-specific wording ('sanctions list', 'OFAC', 'sanctioned by the Treasury', 'debarred'), not a bare 'sanction(s|ed)'.
evidence: zzReview test D: redFlags order [#2 'Judge sanctions...', #1 'convicted...'].
verifyNote: Reproduced. 'Judge sanctions Jane Roe over discovery abuse' (medium) is listed ahead of 'Jane Roe convicted of securities fraud' (high), because a bare 'sanctions' in a headline gives weight 6.
betterFix: Keep the weight-6 floor from LIST_SOURCES and category 'sanctions'. In headlines, match only list wording (OFAC, 'sanctions list', 'sanctioned by the Treasury', debarred, wanted list). A bare 'sanction(s|ed)' falls to the lawsuit weight.

title: Every report of one company matter gets its own timeline row
scenario: Five news records of one lawsuit against the company (match company, litigation, 2023-05-01 to 05-05) become one company matter, but the timeline lists all five. coverageOfFlag holds only red-flag members; company matters and 'if right person' members are not excluded. The duplicates also take up the 60-row cap.
fix: Build coverageOfFlag from the 'more' lists of redFlags, companyMatters and ifRightPerson, and put each matter's lead on the timeline once.
evidence: zzReview test E: companyMatters has 1 entry; the timeline shows 5 rows of the same suit.
verifyNote: Reproduced. Five reports of one company lawsuit form one company matter, but the timeline has five rows, because coverageOfFlag reads only redFlags.more.
betterFix: Build coverageOfFlag from the more lists of redFlags, companyMatters, ifRightPerson and possibleNamesake. Also add the companyMatters and ifRightPerson leads once, so each matter is one timeline row.

title: Bottom line reads "Screens that not enabled on this deployment: ..." and lists nineteen screens in one sentence
scenario: Live run Eric Glyman / Ramp (eval/founder/runs/r10/eric-glyman-ramp.json): the first paragraph of the brief ends with a 120-word list of screens.
fix: In the bottom line give counts only ("9 screens are not enabled here and 10 answered only in part; see Public-record screens") and fix the grammar; the full list belongs in the PUBLIC-RECORD SCREENS section.

title: "the latest funding on record is $30M" when later and larger rounds are in the same report; a funding entry with no citation and a 2016 date for a company founded in 2019
scenario: Same report: companyFacts.funding = Series B $115M (no date), $30M (no date), $2B dated 2016-05-18 with no cites, $300M dated 2021-08-24. The brief calls the undated $30M the latest.
fix: Never call an undated round the latest; order by date; drop any funding entry with no citation or dated before the company was founded (companyFacts.js owner fixes the source; the brief must also guard).

title: UK subsidiaries are each called "the legal name of Ramp"
scenario: WHAT CHECKS OUT lists "Ramp Business UK LTD is the legal name of Ramp on a register entry", the same for Ramp Platform UK LTD and Ramp Business Corporation.
fix: Say "a registered entity of Ramp" and group them in one line; only the entity that files as the issuer or the home-country registration is "the legal name".

title: Company matters from court dockets carry no date, court outcome or what they are about
scenario: "Peters v. Ramp Business Corporation (US Bankruptcy Court, District of Colorado, federal court docket)" with no year.
fix: Show the filing year when the record has one and say when it has none; group the three dockets under one heading.
